newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian army hunts Shining Path military leader.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian army hunts Shining Path military leader.

text.p: The Peruvian army has been deploying 2,000 soldiers in the central Andes since early September to hunt down the military leader of the Shining Path guerrilla group, sources close to the operation said on Tuesday.

In its manoeuvres to surround and close in on Oscar Ramirez Durand, alias "Comrade Feliciano," the army has so far destroyed four training camps and captured 11 rebels. Six guerrillas and three soldiers have also died in ensuing clashes between the security forces and rebels, the sources added.
The Maoist group's leader was believed to be hiding out on the lower slopes of the Andes in central Peru guarded by a battalion of over 50 Shining Path rebels, the sources said.

But anti-terrorist police sources said it was possible that Ramirez had slipped through the ring of soldiers, who were slowed down by booby-traps of excrement-covered stakes and mines laid throughout the operation zone.

Ramirez has gradually come to dominate the Shining Path, which has been greatly weakened since the 1992 capture of its leader Abimael Guzman, and has steered the group to a bloodier course this year, according to security force sources.

After a coordinated series of car-bombs, assassinations and clashes with security forces in August, the country's police chief Antonio Ketin Vidal, who masterminded Guzman's arrest, said the capture of Shining Path's leaders was essential for the group's "dismembering."
Conflicts sparked by the Shining Path and the smaller Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) have cost 30,000 lives and $25 billion in infrastructure damage since 1980.
